title: Restricted Transactional Predictor-Corrector Coupling Window Orchestrator — Architecture Invariant Audit
scope: Owner-side restricted composition audit only; independent qualification and canonical/production admission remain separate gates.
key_findings: Predictor and corrector SWAP trajectories use one captured committed checkpoint and both span the same generic coupling window.
Predictor SWAP and groundwater candidates are discarded and never published.
Corrector publication is preflighted across SWAP candidate, prepared groundwater reservation, prepared ledger handle and next-origin provenance before first irreversible publication.
Exact accepted whole-window bottom exchange from F-GC21P1 is converted to the typed F-GC17 flux pair; terminal bottom flux is not extrapolated over the whole window.
Groundwater flux is assigned as the exact opposite of SWAP flux and the committed interface ledger requires an exact zero conservation residual; no mass tolerance is introduced.
Concrete FMR forcing adaptation uses the typed F-GC17 common-datum head conversion and does not expose solver-private HeadCalc arrays to the orchestrator.
Stable unique ledger identity remains runtime/coupler-owned; F-GC21 does not generate global ledger IDs.
Ledger and groundwater stale/copied/replay/exhaustion semantics remain owned by their admitted components and are rerun by the owner qualification gate.
No direct MODFLOW, tile aggregation, deep-vadose, crash-consistency, distributed-atomicity or throughput claim is made.

invariants.assessment: Uses the admitted common SWAP kernel/runtime interfaces; no use-case-specific calculation kernel.
Orchestrator and adapters contain no file/path/parser/file-unit I/O contract.
Parameters, committed state, forcing, numerical config, coupling origin and result remain explicit separate arguments/types.
Adds only compact coupling origin/result/diagnostic state; immutable physical parameters remain external.
No persistent Newton/Jacobian/constitutive scratch is added to logical columns.
Runtime seam is per logical coupling window and does not prescribe AoS storage or one heavy solver per column.
One committed checkpoint feeds trial predictor/corrector; rejected paths rollback/discard; publication is explicitly preflighted.
Predictor may inform the corrector boundary guess while both physical SWAP trajectories originate from the same committed checkpoint.
Window is generic finite [t0,t1]; no midnight/day/month/year control semantics.
No fixed 00:00-00:00 or one-day coupling window; caller controls finite window length.
Predictor-corrector, rollback, interface residuals, exact flux pairing and transactional publication are explicit runtime functionality.
Uses typed F-GC17 common-datum head residual and exact q_GW=-q_SWAP pairing.
No mass tolerance; accepted exact bottom exchange is ledgered and committed conservation residual must be exactly zero.
Does not remove or hide the kernel interface-sensitivity result; this owner workunit adds orchestration only.
Normal route performs exactly predictor plus corrector full SWAP trajectories; no 6-9-run finite-difference coupling path.
No per-column heavyweight solver ownership is introduced; orchestration remains compatible with batched runtime scheduling.
No 1:1 MODFLOW-cell assumption or area fraction is encoded; tile aggregation remains outside this workunit.
No deep-vadose transfer-zone logic is embedded in SWAP or this coupling-window orchestrator.
No component-transition storage is introduced; exact interface exchange remains explicit for external composition.
Orchestrator targets kernel/runtime contracts rather than one Richards implementation.
Reuses admitted SWAP physics and forcing/kernel seams; no duplicate groundwater or soil-water physics.
Typed FMR adapter maps public hydraulic-head forcing without exposing HeadCalc/private solver arrays to other modules.
Physical profile admission is separate from convergence/numerical policy; restricted PC policy does not silently change physics.
Owner route is bounded to predictor+corrector; nonconvergence requests a smaller outer window with explicit diagnostics.
Reference kernel/backend authority remains available and unmodified; no reference mode is removed.
Route, failure stage, component statuses, convergence, preparation and publication state are explicit diagnostics.
Groundwater coupling state exists only when this runtime component is instantiated; no global optional-state tax is added.
System composition, ledger identity, groundwater service and forcing adapter are supplied by runtime/coupler, not SWAP kernel physics.
No .swp/file/MODFLOW/midnight/day hidden dependency; generic typed contracts are explicit.
This JSON plus owner gate explicitly checks all 30 architecture invariants before any independent/canonical admission claim.

nonclaims: No distributed or crash-consistent atomic transaction claim.
No F-GC20 tile aggregation composition claim.
